chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jaʿfarī, who said:

When I departed from Minā, I intended to stay in Makkah, so I performed the salat in full. Then news came to me from home, and I found no alternative but to go to the home. I did not know whether I should perform in full or shorten, while Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was at that time in Makkah, so I came to him and related the story to him. He said: Return to shortening.

The proper understanding of this report is that he only instructed him to return to shortening because he had not yet performed any of the obligatory salawat. So when his intention changed, his duty became shortening, according to what was explained in the first report. The questioner's statement, 'and I had been performing in full,' is to be understood as referring to supererogatory prayers rather than obligatory ones, because what is considered here is that he must have performed one obligatory prayer in full; at that point it becomes obligatory for him to continue performing in full for the rest of his stay, as was clarified in the first report.

key_terms.التَّمَامِ: performing the salat in full rather than shortened
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat whose legal form is under discussion
key_terms.الصَّلَوَاتِ الْفَرَائِضِ: the obligatory daily prayers that determine the ruling
key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers, not legally determinative here
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: intended residence or staying in a place
key_terms.نِيَّتُهُ: his legal intention regarding residence and travel

ai.seo_question: If a traveler intends to stay ten days and then changes his mind, should he perform salat in full or shorten it?
ai.summary: This report discusses the fiqh ruling for a traveler who intended to remain in Makkah for ten days and therefore began performing salat in full, but then changed his intention before performing any obligatory prayer in full. In that case, his ruling returns to shortening the prayer. The closing explanation clarifies that the binding effect of full prayer begins only after one obligatory prayer has actually been performed in full.
